info.name: firecrawl-integration-test
info.description:
Sources that need a real browser, scraped with Firecrawl instead of being SearXNG engines. All were probed on 2026-10-11; per-source reasoning is in DESIGN.md of the searxng repo.

Two Polish quote sources cross-check each other: biznesradar reports 43.82 and market cap ~25.3bn, parkiet reports the same. biznesradar has the scriptable URL shape (/notowania/{SYMBOL}); parkiet is richer but needs a numeric company id. biznes.pap.pl is news, not quotes.

Deliberately excluded after testing: stooq.pl (robots.txt is User-agent:* / Disallow:/, allow-listed to Googlebot and Bingbot only), Google Finance (renders page chrome but no quote data at any wait), Bloomberg (AAPL:US control returns 500 SCRAPE_ALL_ENGINES_FAILED), gpw.pl (unreachable from this host), and discuss.lifecycle.com via Firecrawl (hangs; that source is a SearXNG engine instead - liferay_forum - so it lives in the other repo).

Run 'Start Crawl' first to populate {{crawlId}} automatically, or set it manually.

request.description: Firecrawl marks /v1/extract deprecated in favor of /v2/scrape. Expect ~40-60s.

item.name: Search Safe Filter (Jev via OpenCode Zen)
item.description: Exercises Jev (TypeSafe) through /v2/search safe:true. lib/search/safe-search.ts asks Jev one noul question per result and drops anything scoring above 0.3. Needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY in .env, forwarded into the container by x-common-env, plus TYPESAFE_MODEL (e.g. jev-1.13 on OpenCode Zen). The last two requests run the same filter at limit 20: the page-size contract (cost, latency, one noul question per result) and the over-filtering guard.

item.description: Guards the opposite failure: Jev over-filtering. The upstream search provider is intermittent, so the query is retried for up to 60s. The strict check, when results do come back, is that no explicit URL survived.

item.name: SearXNG (local search provider)
item.description:
SearXNG is the container /v2/search asks first on this stack. The chain is fire-engine -> SearXNG -> DuckDuckGo (apps/api/src/search/v2/index.ts); with FIRE_ENGINE_BETA_URL unset, SearXNG is the first link and DuckDuckGo only fills in what it missed. These go through Firecrawl and assert the shape apps/api/src/search/v2/searxng.ts builds. SearXNG itself now runs as a separate project (/opt/playground/searxng, container/docker-compose.yml); its own collection (searxng-integration-test) talks to the instance directly, which is how you tell a SearXNG problem apart from a Firecrawl problem.

Knobs: SEARXNG_ENDPOINT in .env (without it Firecrawl never calls SearXNG at all), SEARXNG_ENGINES / SEARXNG_CATEGORIES to narrow the web category, SEARXNG_NEWS_CATEGORIES to replace the news categories (default news), and the SearXNG project's container/core-config/settings.yml, which must keep search.formats [html, json] - without json Firecrawl gets 200 responses carrying no results array.

The folder carries one pre-request guard: a request whose host variable does not resolve to a real URL is skipped with a console warning naming the variable, which is what a shared-link copy (no collection variable, no environment selected) produces.
